title: Fig. 3 analogue — Lower disruption with team size is clearest in the bottom citation-impact half
description: Within-year D percentile (higher means greater disruption) by team size and within-year impact, n=7,997 Columbia works. Citations are strictly postpublication through 23 November 2026. Pointwise 95% design intervals rerank both measures; horizontal line is the 50th percentile, vertical line separates exact sizes and bins. For sizes 1–10, change in mean D percentile per author doubling: bottom half −2.65 [−3.46, −1.88], n=3,299; middle −1.30 [−2.44, 0.27], n=2,503; top tenth +0.18 [−4.05, 2.84], n=462. Top-minus-bottom slope +2.83 [−1.42, 5.66], n=3,761: no support for a stronger decline at high impact.

reviews.summary: The figure is legible and provides a direct test of C3, but it does not substantiate the claim as written. Among teams of 1–10 authors, the decline is clearest in the bottom citation-impact half. The middle and top-group slope intervals include zero, and the top-minus-bottom contrast is too uncertain to conclude that the decline is stronger at high impact.

issues.problem: The title does not distinguish the fitted comparison for teams of 1–10 authors from the descriptive means for larger team-size bins.
issues.fix: Qualify the title with ‘among teams of 1–10 authors’ or state in the caption that the larger bins are shown descriptively and are not included in the slope comparison.

issues.problem: The caption explains that both measures are reranked but does not say how sampling weights enter the ranks, plotted means, and slopes. The legend gives impact-group totals but not the counts behind individual points.
issues.fix: State which estimates use sampling weights, label the reported n values as observed counts, and point readers to T52 for counts by team size and impact group.
